13:20.race_name: Ryanair Mares' Novices' Hurdle (Grade 2) (Registered As The Dawn Run mares' Novices' Hurdle) (GBB)

runners.comment: Dual French winner but beaten fair and square on British debut at Taunton
runners.name: Al Fonce
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 5yo whose two French wins (2m1f/2m3f) were on heavy ground; good ground when she was beaten fair and square in a Listed race at Taunton in December (behind St Irene) and that form gives her no right to be mixing it with the best of these.

runners.comment: Held by Bambino Fever on bumper form but she has progressed well over hurdles
runners.name: Amen Kate
runners.owner: Ciaran John Mooney & John Francis Ryan
runners.spotlight: Useful bumper form but hammered by Bambino Fever when they once clashed in that scene; steadily progressive hurdler and her trainer targeted this race straight after she won a Listed race at Thurles in December (yielding); probably playing for the places, however.

runners.comment: Star bumper performer; beaten on hurdling debut but impressive enough last time
runners.name: Bambino Fever
runners.spotlight: Top of the pops last season in bumpers, beating the boys in the big one here (good to soft) before making it 4-4 in that sphere at Punchestown where her customary turbo kicked in when it mattered; her stable was quiet when she was surprisingly floored by Oldschool Outlaw on her hurdling debut and she then made no mistake from the front at Fairyhouse (2m2f, yielding) where her jumping was quick and accurate; tongue-tie is added; only six and she's probably still progressing; proven on the track, she'll take some beating.

runners.comment: Progressing but has to unearth something from somewhere to threaten at this loftier level
runners.name: Blue Velvet
runners.spotlight: Held by Bambino Fever on bumper form but she has raised her game in maiden hurdles at Punchestown (heavy; won a bumper on good), finishing second to a good horse before accounting for a subsequent Leopardstown maiden winner with the pair in isolation; she'll need to unearth something from somewhere to threaten at this loftier level.

runners.comment: Runner-up in a Grade 1 last time and she's back against her own sex here; respected
runners.name: Carrigmoornaspruce
runners.spotlight: Beaten about 13l by Bambino Fever in a bumper but she won three of those, including a Grade 3 at Punchestown (yielding); no surprise to see her doing well over hurdles and the defeats have come in a Grade 3 at Down Royal (won by Full Of Life who dictated) and a Grade 1 at Leopardstown where she was left in second at the final flight behind smart gelding Skylight Hustle; she's back against her own sex here and rates solid each-way material.

runners.comment: Has 12l to find with Echoing Silence on their Punchestown meeting in December
runners.name: Chosen Comrade
runners.spotlight: Point, bumper and maiden hurdle winner who has 12l to find with Echoing Silence on their Punchestown meeting in December and there were no clear excuses, other than the heavy ground perhaps finding her out; even if happier on this surface (she has won on good to yielding and yielding to soft), she'll probably be feeling the heat when it matters.

runners.comment: 0-13 in France but was useful; won a weak race at Ludlow; may need the mud
runners.name: Diamond Du Berlais
runners.spotlight: 0-13 in France but she contested some warm races and earned placed honours at Grade 2 and 3 level; joined current connections for 160,000euros and did what was expected of her in a weak maiden at Ludlow (2m5f, soft) for which she was long odds-on and won accordingly; may need plenty of ease underfoot to be at her best and even a peak effort will probably see her come up short.

runners.breeder: Exors Of The Late G Rothwell
runners.comment: Improving mare with form over further, which hasn't been a negative in this race
runners.name: Echoing Silence
runners.spotlight: From a yard that's won two of the last five renewals of this; it was a useful maiden she won easily at Cork (2m4f, yielding) and she followed up in a 2m3f Listed event at Punchestown despite not being in love with the heavy ground (according to her trainer); the runner-up Switch From Diesel gave Bambino Fever something to think about in two bumpers last season, so that latest form heightens interest in this mare; the stable's winner 12 months ago was also dropping back in distance and returning from a similar break; very much one to bear in mind.

runners.comment: Determined in keeping Carrigmoornaspruce at bay in a Grade 3 last time in October
runners.name: Full Of Life
runners.spotlight: A stablemate of Echoing Silence; strike-rate of 2-6 over hurdles wouldn't be in keeping with a typical winner of this race, and neither would the fact that she's already tried fences (0-2); however, she made all in a Grade 3 at Down Royal in late October (2m1f, good to yielding) and was determined in keeping Carrigmoornaspruce at bay; could run well.

runners.breeder: Margaret Treacy On His Own Stables
runners.comment: Many flights were omitted when she won at Naas, so she lacks hurdling experience
runners.name: Future Prospect
runners.spotlight: Cost £150,000 at the sale on the eve of the Gold Cup two years ago; hooded for last three races; looks very vulnerable on bumper form and she lacks experience over hurdles, as several flights were omitted when she beat a big field at Naas (2m, yielding); the runner-up is now 0-5 over hurdles; only one previous winner of this had raced once over hurdles; unconvincing.

runners.comment: 2-3 over hurdles but the Warwick win is no shining advertisement for her prospects
runners.name: Jackie Hobbs
runners.spotlight: Point and dual bumper winner; consistent without being strikingly progressive in going 2-3 over hurdles and the form of her latest win at Warwick (2m3f, good to soft) is no shining advertisement for her prospects.

runners.comment: Grade 2 winner; likeable attitude but that takes you only so far; cheekpieces added
runners.name: Kingston Queen
runners.spotlight: Won two bumpers and was third in the Grade 2 for mares at the Grand National meeting; her only defeat over hurdles came in a race won by Old Park Star and she was a game winner of a Grade 2 at Warwick last time, beating White Noise (2m3f, heavy; fine on good to soft); has a likeable attitude but that takes you only so far; cheekpieces are turned to; others preferred.

runners.breeder: Franklin Finance & S Vidal & E Ribard
runners.comment: Stable won this three years ago with a mare who brought a similar level of form
runners.name: La Conquiere
runners.spotlight: Had some of these behind when runner-up in the Grade 2 bumper for mares at Aintree last April; has taken her form to a higher level over hurdles, impressing in a Listed race at Newbury and not disgraced in defeat behind a talented older mare in a messy Grade 2 at Ascot (again on soft; has won on good); her form is roughly on a par with what You Wear It Well brought here when successful for the same yard three years ago; each-way claims.

runners.breeder: Mrs A Fernandes-Thireau & Mrs M Drion
runners.comment: Did well in France; highly tried here on stable debut and market vibes haven't been strong
runners.name: Louve DIrlande
runners.spotlight: Flat, bumper and hurdle winner in France where her only defeat came in a 1m4f Grade 1 bumper, which was also the only time she's not sported a hood; hurled into the deep end here by new connections and there doesn't appear to be a wave of expectation behind her.

runners.comment: Took the scalp of Bambino Fever on hurdle debut and then easily won a Grade 3
runners.name: Oldschool Outlaw
runners.spotlight: Behind some of these in Aintree bumper last April but has left that form behind since joining Gordon Elliott; as was also the case with Bambino Fever, it was her debut over hurdles when narrowly repelling that mare at Naas, and she followed up with a super-stylish display in adding a Grade 3 at Fairyhouse (2m2f); this hasn't been a lucky race for Gordon Elliott but this mare's star is on the rise and her claims are crystal clear, so long as she doesn't need the soft or heavy ground on which her improvement has come.

runners.breeder: S A S Ecurie X & Mr Yannick Fouin
runners.comment: Couldn't hold a candle to Oldschool Outlaw when returned to Graded company at Fairyhouse
runners.name: Place De La Nation
runners.spotlight: Cracking effort for a maiden to finish fifth in last season's Triumph; won her first two this campaign, though was long odds-on for both (2m6f/2m) and she couldn't hold a candle to Oldschool Outlaw when returned to Graded company at Fairyhouse (2m2f); it takes some imagination to envisage her reversing those placings.

runners.comment: Wetherby maiden winner; she doesn't have the form or the profile for this
runners.name: Scavengers Reign
runners.spotlight: Wetherby maiden winner who has been beaten in her other four races over hurdles; she doesn't have the form or the profile for this.

runners.comment: Listed winner but needs a career best by some almighty margin to be in the shake-up
runners.name: St Irene
runners.spotlight: Limited appeal on bumper exploits but those were for a different yard and she's looked highly progressive over hurdles in the West Country, the latest win in a Listed race; has earned herself a crack at this but she'll need a career best by some almighty margin to be in the shake-up.

runners.comment: Second in a 2m3f Grade last time; probably needs that trip or even further ideally
runners.name: White Noise
runners.spotlight: Tongue tied for her last two starts; her winning spree ended when narrowly foiled by Kingston Queen in a Grade 2 at Warwick last month (2m3f, heavy) and she probably needs that trip or even further ideally.

runners.breeder: S A R L Haras De Saint Faust Et Al
runners.comment: 4yo; light on experience but looked good at Thurles and she's clearly talented
runners.name: Charme De Faust
runners.spotlight: One of three fillies in the race and 4yos are 0-9 in this, though only one traded at shorter than 20-1; Paul Townend was complimentary about all parts of her game after she won a Thurles maiden (2m, heavy) with her head in her chest; whether she's wise enough after just two runs for a race of this nature is questionable but she's clearly talented.

runners.comment: 4-4; dangerous to leave out of calculations without knowing the ceiling of her ability
runners.name: Manganese
runners.spotlight: 4yo; French bumper winner who was entered in the Fred Winter on Tuesday but missed the cut; unbeaten hurdler and took the rise in class in her stride when narrowly too good for a smart subsequent winner, at Doncaster in January (Listed; soft; has won on good to soft); dangerous to leave out of calculations without knowing the ceiling of her ability.

runners.comment: Smart in France; has the 4yo allowance and there appears to be some confidence behind her
runners.name: Mille Et Une Vies
runners.spotlight: Showed significant promise in much respected company in all her three defeats in France last spring (very soft or heavy); has reportedly worked well at her new home and there appears to be some confidence behind her armed with a 10lb age allowance.

14:00.race_name: Jack Richards Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (Grade 2) (Registered As The Golden Miller) (GBB Race)

runners.breeder: Scea De Maulepaire & M C De Saint Seine
runners.comment: Useful sort who has Graded form but likely needs improvement to defy top weight
runners.name: Gold Dancer
runners.spotlight: Non-stayer over 3m on heavy ground last time; consistent form otherwise this term features two Grade 3 wins and a couple of 8l seconds at Grade 1 level; useful sort but doesn't necessarily look well treated and likely needs improvement to defy top weight in this hot handicap.

runners.comment: Front-runner; first past the post in all six starts over 2m4f, latest in Sandown Grade 1
runners.name: Sixmilebridge
runners.spotlight: Front-runner who has finished first past the post in all six attempts over 2m4f (disqualified on one occasion due to banned substance); bagged Grade 1 honours in the Scilly Isles at Sandown (soft) most recently, following up his easy success over this C&D (good to soft) and taking chase record to 3-3; sticks to this trip instead of going for the Arkle or Brown Advisory; still has something to prove in a big field and isn't sure to get an easy lead but otherwise brings several selling points.

runners.comment: Consistent; won the 2024 Supreme in sole Cheltenham attempt; mark is attractive; solid
runners.name: Slade Steel
runners.spotlight: Has form on most types of ground; consistent sort who has never finished out of the first three in his completed starts; broadly suffering from a frustrating bout of seconditis since switched to chasing (2m4f/3m) but this return to Cheltenham may prove the cure, as he won the 2024 Supreme in sole attempt at this venue; major Irish stable landed this corresponding prize in 2019; on an attractive mark and holds solid claims.

runners.comment: Very similar type to last year's winner Caldwell Potter for same connections; respected
runners.name: Regents Stroll
runners.spotlight: Nephew of Denman; unraced on heavy, acts on any other ground; cost £660,000 at a dispersal sale at one point, proved a smart novice hurdler and has picked up C&D experience (latest start) en route to this prize, making him virtually a carbon copy of last year's winner Caldwell Potter for the same connections; has a broadly solid overall record to boot, including form figures of 312 since switched to fences, and likely remains capable of further progress; very strong credentials.

runners.comment: Needs to resume progress but has big-field handicap experience; cheekpieces added
runners.name: Ol Man Dingle
runners.spotlight: Returns from a layoff, having shown all of his chase form in the autumn, winning twice (including 2m4f Grade 3) prior to a form-dip in Fairyhouse Grade 1; needs to resume progress but has big-field handicap experience, namely a good effort over hurdles at the 2025 Dublin Racing Festival; cheekpieces added.

runners.comment: Recorded a career-best RPR with comfortable win at Gowran; peaking at the right time
runners.name: King Alexander
runners.spotlight: Came up well short in the 2m5f handicap hurdle at this meeting last year but may fare better in this return visit as he's still unexposed over fences and has a solid record since switched to this sphere; comfortably justified favouritism at Gowran Park (2m3f) most recently, producing a career-best RPR; peaking at the right time.

runners.comment: Latest effort has been franked by the smart winner since; may be ready to peak
runners.name: Wingmen
runners.spotlight: Seems versatile as regards ground; has consistent form since switched to chasing and latest effort has been franked by the smart winner since; something to find with Slade Steel on Navan running (2m4f) the time before but may be ready to peak and complete a full set by adding to his point, bumper and hurdle wins; one to consider.

runners.breeder: S A S Elevage Michel Rivaillon
runners.comment: Three placed efforts over fences set him up nicely for a crack at this handicap
runners.name: Kiss Will
runners.spotlight: Low-mileage 6yo whose hurdles form comprised 2m/3m wins (including Listed) either side of a comprehensive defeat in the Turners at the 2025 Cheltenham Festival; faces a more realistic task in a handicap back here and three placed efforts over fences, the latest a good one at Punchestown, set him up nicely for a crack at this prize.

runners.comment: Interesting sort, being related to Tully East who won this corresponding race in 2017
runners.name: Moon Rocket
runners.spotlight: Campaigned mainly over 3m; form dipped in Grade 2 most recently; had wind surgery since and now goes in tongue-tie; comfortably beat his three rivals at Doncaster (chase debut; good to soft) in sole handicap attempt and although this is a stiffer assignment he's interesting from a pedigree angle, being related to Tully East who won this corresponding race in 2017.

runners.comment: Good strike-rate and gained latest success in a C&D event of high significance; big player
runners.name: Jordans Cross
runners.spotlight: Has a record of 5-8 overall and 3-4 since switched to chasing; looked a serious threat to stablemate Kdeux Saint Fray when final-fence faller on the Old course here (2m4f) in November; rallied well for a couple of narrow wins since, latest on Trials day in the C&D novice handicap (soft) that has been such a good pointer to this race and indeed this meeting in general; appears very likely to finish strongly and continue his progress; big player.

runners.comment: Remains open to further improvement and the return to 2m4f promises to suit; major player
runners.name: Meetmebythesea
runners.spotlight: Has the same strike-rate as Jordans Cross, being 5-8 overall; struggled in the Game Spirit when bidding to take chase record to 3-3; faces a more suitable assignment in this contest and although he has raced mainly at about 2m, the return to 2m4f promises to suit; good third in major novice handicap hurdle at Sandown (good to soft) in sole attempt over this distance; major contender, with further improvement still plausible.

runners.comment: Has failed to back up the form of his Galway win (chase debut); less solid than others
runners.name: Intense Approach
runners.spotlight: Prevailed in a big field at Galway (2m6f, good) on chase debut but has failed to back up that form since and was particularly disappointing in October when bidding for a second win at the Cheltenham Showcase meeting; wears first-time headgear; less solid than others.

runners.comment: Low-mileage 5yo who won well last time; possibilities provided he stays this new trip
runners.name: Stencil
runners.spotlight: Trained in France but campaigned exclusively in British races since the start of last year, most recently opening his chase account in Chepstow event (2m, soft) having settled better than usual; form of that ready success has been franked by the runner-up since; hood worn the last twice is retained; this low-mileage 5yo remains open to further progress and has possibilities provided he stays the new trip; bids to atone for his flop when favourite for the Fred Winter at this meeting 12 months ago.

runners.comment: Not disgraced in the Reynoldstown over 3m; record of 4-4 at 2m3f-2m5f; could go well
runners.name: Western Knight
runners.spotlight: Failed to complete a hat-trick but was far from discredited at Ascot (3m, good to soft) last time in the Reynoldstown, which was won 12 months earlier by a stablemate who subsequently finished second in the Ultima at this meeting; may have more to offer back down in distance, being 4-4 at 2m3f-2m5f; the tea leaves are signalling that he'll run well.

runners.comment: Ran creditably in Grade 2 last time but has been punished with another rise in his mark
runners.name: Old Cowboy
runners.spotlight: Held a narrow advantage when falling two out at Kempton in January; ran creditably in Grade 2 there (again over 2m4f) since but has been punished with another rise in his mark, which is now a stone higher than when scoring at Newbury in December; others look better handicapped.

runners.breeder: Dr V Bernard Stoffel & Mr Vincent Leroy
runners.comment: Record of 121 since joining new yard and switched to chasing; lightly raced and improving
runners.name: The Bluesman
runners.spotlight: Campaigned mostly on soft/good to soft; bumper/hurdles winner for Paul Nicholls; record of 121 (over 2m4f) since joining new yard and switched to chasing, both wins gained in comfortable fashion, latest at Haydock; could make some waves in these deeper waters, being a lightly raced and improving contender.

runners.comment: Has inconsistent form since switched to chasing; not certain to back up latest effort
runners.name: Wheres My Jet
runners.spotlight: Has inconsistent form since switched to chasing and two non-completions were caused by bad mistakes; fared best of the eight runners from his yard in competitive handicap at the Dublin Racing Festival (2m5f) most recently but isn't certain to back up that effort.

runners.comment: Has notable Cheltenham form but possibly isn't crying out for this drop back to 2m4f
runners.name: Kdeux Saint Fray
runners.spotlight: Rather fortuitous winner on the Old course here (2m4f, soft) in November as stablemate Jordans Cross looked a massive threat when falling; finished 5l behind that rival in the rematch over C&D on Trials day, shaping as if ready for a crack at further; duly ran well, despite jumping left at times, in major 3m handicap at right-handed Kempton (good to soft) since; brings notable form but possibly isn't crying out for the drop back in trip; 1lb out of weights.

runners.comment: Again faces stronger candidates from his own yard; overall record is only 2-15
runners.name: Dr Eggman
runners.spotlight: Finished third behind shorter-priced stablemates in last two outings and is again facing stronger candidates from his own yard, before even considering the many other dangers; overall record of just 2-15 reflects that he hasn't progressed as well as expected; 2lb out of the handicap.

runners.comment: Has performed well at Chepstow since switched to chasing but this is a stiffer task
runners.name: Ben Solo
runners.spotlight: Has shown most of his form on Welsh tracks, latterly Chepstow since switched to chasing; ran well when bidding for a 2m3f double and was in a narrow lead, albeit being challenged, when falling three out last time; faces a much stiffer task from 5lb out of the weights at this level.

14:40.race_name: Close Brothers Mares' Hurdle (Registered As The David Nicholson Mares' Hurdle) (Grade 1) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Likeable but behind Wodhooh and Feet Of A Dancer (twice) in recent races
runners.name: Dream On Baby
runners.spotlight: Steadily progressive; won Listed event at Kempton (2m5f, good) in November; has advanced her form in defeat since, finishing third to Wodhooh and Feet Of A Dancer in Grade 3 at Leopardstown (2m4f, good/yielding) over Christmas before getting outstayed by the latter in a 3m Grade 2 at Doncaster (soft) in January; likeable but surely far more a place than win contender.

runners.comment: Listed and Grade 2 winner this season but beaten by Wodhooh at Leopardstown in between
runners.name: Feet Of A Dancer
runners.spotlight: Consistent type; fourth in the Pertemps Final at this meeting last year and has taken her form to an even higher level this term, winning Listed race at Punchestown (2m2f, soft to heavy) and Grade 2 at Doncaster (3m, soft); beat Dream On Baby by 2l in the latter, with Jetara a further 7l back in third; however, Wodhooh gave her 8lb and a beating (just over 2l) at Leopardstown in between, so it's tough to see how she can turn the tables off levels.

runners.breeder: S C E A Ecurie La Grugerie
runners.comment: Two Grade 1 hurdle wins; Grade 2 novice chase win latest; 2nd last year; sure to go well
runners.name: Jade De Grugy
runners.spotlight: 5-7 over hurdles; second to stablemate Lossiemouth in this last year before a Grade 1 win at the Punchestown festival, her second success at the top level; has taken well to fences this winter, finishing second in Limerick Grade 2 over Christmas before going one better in similar company at Thurles (2m5f, yielding) in January; most consistent and looks sure to go well back hurdling.

runners.comment: 4th last year; operating a little below her best this term; blinkers replace cheekpieces
runners.name: Jetara
runners.spotlight: Smart mare who was an 11l fourth to Lossiemouth in this 12 months ago before finishing third in 3m Grade 1s at Aintree and Punchestown later in the spring; hasn't quite hit the same heights this season, including 9l third to Feet Of A Dancer and Dream On Baby in Doncaster Grade 2 latest; vulnerable even if back to her very best in a change of headgear (first-time blinkers replace cheekpieces).

runners.comment: Useful but has plenty to find on form
runners.name: Sunset Marquesa
runners.spotlight: Followed a clearcut handicap win at Sandown (2m4f, soft) with a good fourth to Nurse Susan in a Listed event there in January; another sound effort when a rallying third of four in 2m Ascot mares' Grade 2 (soft) since; the return to further will suit but she has plenty to find on form.

runners.comment: Third to Lossiemouth last year; has run well in defeat this term; each-way player again
runners.name: Take No Chances
runners.spotlight: Won Grade 2 mares' event at Ascot before finishing third to Lossiemouth in this and the Aintree Hurdle (Wodhooh 8l ahead in second) last spring; has slightly bettered those RPRs in defeat on all four outings this season and she's an each-way player again.

runners.comment: 9-10 over hurdles, including two C&D wins; two Graded wins this term; again hard to beat
runners.name: Wodhooh
runners.spotlight: Has won nine of her ten hurdle starts (including last year's Martin Pipe over C&D), with her only defeat coming at the hands of Lossiemouth in the Grade 1 Aintree Hurdle (2m4f, good to soft) last spring; has looked every bit as good when landing Grade 2 Ascot Hurdle (2m3f, good to soft) and a 2m4f Grade 3 at Leopardstown's Christmas meeting (gave weight and beat Feet Of A Dancer just over 2l) this season; will be hard to beat.

runners.comment: 14l third to Teahupoo in Christmas Hurdle; may again be vulnerable to stronger stayers
runners.name: Ballyburn
runners.spotlight: Displayed superstar potential when easily winning the 2m5f Grade 1 novice hurdle here in 2024; mixed campaign over fences last term and he's reverted to hurdles this season, going very close behind Teahupoo in Grade 1 Hatton's Grace (2m4f, yielding to soft) before 14l third to that rival in Grade 1 Christmas Hurdle (2m7f, good to yielding); the first-time hood could help this headstrong 8yo settle but he may again be vulnerable to stronger stayers.

runners.comment: Won this last year and excellent record at Cheltenham means he has to be in calculations
runners.name: Bob Olinger
runners.spotlight: Now 11 but he was as good as ever last March when winning this race by nearly 2l from Teahupoo (good to soft; also effective on soft); respectable second to that rival at Leopardstown in December on sole run this season and his excellent record at Cheltenham means he has to be in calculations.

runners.comment: Won the Pertemps Final over C&D last March but 0-4 in Graded races in current campaign
runners.name: Doddiethegreat
runners.spotlight: Won the Pertemps Final Handicap over C&D (good to soft) last March and he's performed respectably in Graded races this term, most recently third of six over C&D behind Ma Shantou and Impose Toi (soft; jockey dropped whip after final flight); it's possible he'll produce his best performance of the season now he's back into a bigger field over a C&D that clearly suits, but he'll probably still come up short; blinkers replace cheekpieces.

runners.comment: Won Grade 2 Rendlesham last February but hasn't matched that form before or since
runners.name: Gwennie May Boy
runners.spotlight: Impressive in Grade 2 Rendlesham at Haydock (3m, good to soft) last February but hasn't matched that form before or since; well beaten on final two runs for Dan Skelton last April and same story this term on both outings for Olly Murphy; starts out for another new yard and is hard to fancy.

runners.comment: 2023 King George winner; now 11; soundly beaten 5th of 7 in Long Distance Hurdle last time
runners.name: Hewick
runners.spotlight: Career highlight when winning the 2023 King George and he was running well when falling two out in the Gold Cup here that year; won two conditions hurdles last year; soundly beaten behind Impose Toi in Grade 2 Long Distance Hurdle at Newbury (3m, soft) in November last time and, although he's had a wind op and better ground may aid his cause, this 11yo looks up against it.

runners.comment: Grade 2 win in January but this 11yo has found Grade 1 races tough over the last 12 months
runners.name: Home By The Lee
runners.spotlight: Two-time Grade 1 winner, latterly in 2024, who landed the Grade 2 Galmoy Hurdle at Gowran Park in January, showing he retains considerable spark at the age of 11; he's run well in this race previously but has found Grade 1 races tough over the last 12 months; could have same problem today.

runners.breeder: H Fowler A Frost & C Longsdon
runners.comment: Very lightly raced 6yo; has the potential to take high rank in the staying hurdle division
runners.name: Honesty Policy
runners.spotlight: Stayed on well to win 2m4f Grade 1 novice hurdle at Aintree (good) last April and suited by the step up in trip when close second in Grade 1 at Punchestown (3m, yielding) later that month, when clear with Jasmin De Vaux who was impressive in the Albert Bartlett here previously; promising third behind Impose Toi in the Grade 1 Long Walk at Ascot (3m, good to soft) in December on sole run this winter, and this very lightly raced 6yo has the potential to take high rank in the staying hurdle division.

runners.comment: Grade 1 Long Walk winner; capable of better than he showed when runner-up in the Cleeve
runners.name: Impose Toi
runners.spotlight: Handicap runner-up at last year's Festival; made it 3-3 over staying trips in the Grade 1 Long Walk at Ascot (3m, good to soft) in December; not seen to same effect when 7l second to Ma Shantou in the Grade 2 Cleeve Hurdle over C&D in January but was conceding 6lb to the winner and the soft going perhaps wasn't ideal; could have a part to play if bouncing back to his best.

runners.comment: Powered clear to win the Grade 2 Relkeel here over an extended 2m4f; now tackles new trip
runners.name: Kabral Du Mathan
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 6yo who won a handicap at Haydock (2m3f, good to soft) in November on stable debut and followed up in the Grade 2 Relkeel Hurdle here (extended 2m4f, good) on New Year's Day, again with plenty in hand; this is a tough race in which to try to prove his stamina but he powered clear up the hill last time and could be a contender if seeing out this new trip.

runners.comment: Highly progressive 7yo who won Grade 2 Cleeve Hurdle over C&D in January by 7l; big chance
runners.name: Ma Shantou
runners.spotlight: Two handicap wins here this season (3m, good) and he took the rise in grade in his stride to win the Grade 2 Cleeve Hurdle over C&D (soft) in January; the 7l runner-up Impose Toi was giving him 6lb and perhaps wasn't at his best, but this highly progressive 7yo was impressive nevertheless; his profile is not dissimilar to that of Paisley Park, who won the Cleeve for this yard in 2019 before landing this race; very much one to be interested in.

runners.breeder: S C E A Haras Du Hoguenet Et Al
runners.comment: He has a very strong record in this race, winning it in 2024, and is a leading player
runners.name: Teahupoo
runners.spotlight: He has a very strong record in this race with a close third in 2023 (soft), a win in 2024 (soft) and a solid second to Bob Olinger 12 months ago (good to soft); won three Grade 1s since, latest the Christmas Hurdle at Leopardstown (2m7f, good to yielding) where he beat Bob Olinger by 7l (albeit with that rival lacking a recent outing, unlike this fellow); has had a break prior to running in this race in each of the last two seasons; leading player.

16:00.race_name: Ryanair Chase (Registered As The Festival Trophy) (Grade 1) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Won and touched off in last two King Georges but soundly beaten at last two Festivals
runners.name: Banbridge
runners.spotlight: Won the Martin Pipe over hurdles at this meeting in 2022 as well as a novice chase here that year, but Kempton is where his heart lies, having won the Grade 1 King George (3m, good) in 2024 and gone desperately close in the same race (first-time visor, retained here) on Boxing Day; however, he's been beaten a long way out at the last two Festivals, in this race and the Gold Cup, and a flat track may now be ideal; has something to prove.

runners.comment: Two Grade 1 wins as a novice chaser last season; out of sorts; lots to find at the weights
runners.name: Croke Park
runners.spotlight: Two Grade 1 wins as a novice chaser last season, over 2m4f (yielding) and about 3m (good to yielding), but nothing he's achieved this winter, behind Heart Wood on two occasions, and in a Leopardstown handicap last month, suggests he can play a part on these unfavourable terms.

runners.comment: Won Grade 1s at the last two Festivals, including this race; set fair to dominate again
runners.name: Fact To File
runners.spotlight: He's run at the last three Festivals, finishing runner-up in the bumper, winning the Brown Advisory novice chase (about 3m) and at the peak of his powers when beating Heart Wood in this race last year (good to soft); had an undesirably hard race when narrowly beaten by Gaelic Warrior at Punchestown in November and he was never on his game in the King George at Kempton on Boxing Day; however, he looked his old self for the first time this winter when beating a top-class field in the Irish Gold Cup at Leopardstown (about 3m, soft) in February and looks set fair to dominate today's opposition.

runners.comment: Well-held second to Fact To File in this race last year; another place is achievable
runners.name: Heart Wood
runners.spotlight: Has yet to win at above Grade 3 level although he only just failed against Croke Park in a less competitive Grade 1 than this at Fairyhouse (2m4f, yielding) in December 2024; he enjoyed his front-running role when winning at Tramore (2m7f, soft) in January when never seriously challenged and it's likely he will be ridden more prominently today than when no match for Fact To File in this race (good to soft) last March; he will still do well to fend off that winner but another place is perfectly achievable.

runners.breeder: S C E A Haras De Peyre & Mme Pascale Pa
runners.comment: Festival winner over hurdles; won Grade 1 chase last April; needs more for the win
runners.name: Impaire Et Passe
runners.spotlight: A fine hurdler whose three Grade 1 wins included the Ballymore at this meeting in 2023; has reached the same standard over fences, winning at the top level at Aintree (about 2m4f, good to soft; first-time cheekpieces) last April, and he was ultimately quite convincing in a tactical race at Gowran (about 2m3f, heavy) last month; his form doesn't yet match that of stablemate Fact To File but he is considered for a place.

runners.comment: Course winner; top-class two-miler who is 3-3 at about 2m5f, staying on well latest
runners.name: Jonbon
runners.spotlight: Has maintained an incredibly high standard in Grade 1s over 2m but, although he has won here, his rare reverses have come on this track; no longer quite the speedster he used to be at 2m and the extra stamina test was a help when winning at Ascot (about 2m5f, good to soft) last month, where he could have settled for second had his enduring will to win not come to his aid; now defends a strike-rate of 3-3 at about this trip but it remains to be seen whether he can rise to this very big occasion.

runners.comment: Won 2m4f handicap chase latest; much more to do here and well held at 3 previous Festivals
runners.name: JPR One
runners.spotlight: Made short work of conceding plenty of weight in his first 2m4f chase - a Musselburgh handicap (good to soft) in January - and with his best sibling staying 3m well, there's a fair chance he'll cope with this much stiffer test at the trip; however, his three previous Festival runs, including a 2m handicap last year, suggest he'll be pushed to play a part in this company.

runners.comment: Has plenty to find at the weights; well adrift behind Fact To File in this last year
runners.name: Master Chewy
runners.spotlight: Finished a creditable close second of three finishers in a Grade 2 at Kempton (about 2m4f, good) in January but he's an infrequent winner and it's two years since he ran well in a Grade 1 (not far away when falling two out in the Arkle here, then touched off at Aintree); well adrift in this race last year and there's no reason to expect much better today.

runners.comment: Ready winner of C&D handicap in January; Grade 1 company likely to be beyond him again
runners.name: Matata
runners.spotlight: Nearly all races at around 2m1f and the step up to 2m4f was clearly a stretch behind Jonbon in an Aintree Grade 1 last April; coped better with the trip when a convincing winner of a C&D handicap (good; has won on soft) in January but a lesser effort followed at Windsor and he aims a lot higher here.

16:40.race_name: Pertemps Network Final Handicap Hurdle (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: 2m6f-3m has proved just the ticket this winter with three wins; tough customer
runners.name: Staffordshire Knot
runners.spotlight: Never got seriously involved when ninth in the 2m5f handicap at last year's Festival; 2m6f-3m has proved just the ticket this winter with three wins (including the Punchestown qualifier) and a second, with last two outings in Grade 2; they were all in the mud but good to soft was fine earlier in career; tough customer and Gordon Elliott won this three times in a row not so long ago, twice with Sire Du Berlais among the topweights.

runners.comment: Cheltenham regular; back up 2lb to his career-high mark but probably not far away
runners.name: Gowel Road
runners.spotlight: Can front-run; Cheltenham regular, where he won a 3m Grade 2 last January; sixth in this in 2024 and ran creditably here on three of his first five starts this season, before a big run under Toby McCain-Mitchell at Chepstow 19 days ago; back up 2lb to his career-high mark but probably not far away.

runners.comment: Major chance after his second to Ma Shantou here and a win in valuable race at Haydock
runners.name: Electric Mason
runners.owner: KTDA Racing And Mrs Nicola Morris
runners.spotlight: Soundly beaten here in the Martin Pipe 12 months ago but second of 17 to today's Grade 1 Stayers' hopeful Ma Shantou back here (3m, good) in October; improved to win valuable race in another big field at Haydock (3m, good to soft) in November and should be raring to go today, with major chance.

runners.comment: Two wins this term and a good 2nd here; progressive 7yo who has to be taken seriously
runners.name: Ace Of Spades
runners.spotlight: Won two of his four starts this term and stayed on well for second to today's Grade 1 Stayers' candidate Ma Shantou here (3m, good) on New Year's Day on penultimate start; latest was a Huntingdon win (3m1f, soft) and he's now 5lb higher but this progressive 7yo has to be taken seriously.

runners.comment: Surged back to form when a recent, close second at Naas (2m7f, heavy) in second-time visor
runners.name: Minella Sixo
runners.spotlight: Second here (on good) early as novice but tailed off in the Martin Pipe last March; better over this sort of trip and surged back to form when a close second to Melbourne Shamrock in the Naas qualifier (2m7f, heavy) 18 days ago in a second-time visor, staying on strongly from off pace; requires better to justify this British mark but needs a second look for trainer who's done well in this race.

runners.breeder: Mrs M Pallot & Mr J C Pallot
runners.comment: Soft ground has probably helped but he keeps finding more and probably has deeper reserves
runners.name: Kikijo
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 6yo who has made a big splash on his switch back to hurdling this season, ridden prominently when winning over about 3m at Cheltenham and Sandown (under Callum Pritchard last time); up another 8lb today; those wins were on soft ground, which probably helped him, but he keeps finding more and probably has deeper reserves, so cannot be passed over at all lightly.

runners.comment: Promising on return; subsequent runs not hard to forgive; favourite for this for some time
runners.name: Supremely West
runners.spotlight: No ground issues; promising late gains when third of 17 on stable debut in the Cheltenham qualifier in October; not so hot since but those runs aren't hard to forgive (the latest was over just 2m4f) and he's now 2lb lower than on that eye-catching reappearance; trainer is a dab hand in these Festival handicaps and this 8yo has been favourite for this race for some time.

runners.comment: 5-5 for Paul Nicholls, finishing off the opposition in storming fashion; shortlisted
runners.name: Absolutely Doyen
runners.spotlight: 5-5 for Paul Nicholls (good/good to soft) and the last three of those races were over 3m, including in the Wincanton qualifier; racking up the wins would be a highly unusual profile for a Pertemps Final winner but he keeps finishing off the opposition in storming fashion and could easily still have more to give; on the shortlist.

runners.comment: Third run on the comeback trail; well handicapped if back to his best form last winter
runners.name: Red Dirt Road
runners.spotlight: Two wins last winter, latterly at Sandown (extended 2m7f, heavy; by 8l making all); pulled up on next two starts, with 322 days off in between, but fourth in the Haydock qualifier last month was a big step back in the right direction; now needs to make another but he's only 1lb higher than at Sandown.

runners.comment: Not quite so good this term; did not shout stamina when upped to 3m for last two outings
runners.name: Classic King
runners.spotlight: Did well at 2m3f-2m5f when reverting to hurdles for his last three starts last season; not quite so good this term and he did not shout stamina when upped to 3m for last two outings; others have more compelling claims.

runners.comment: Never better than on last three starts; needs to resume improvement in this hot handicap
runners.name: Lavida Adiva
runners.spotlight: Never better than on her last three starts, winning a Listed mares' hurdle at Doncaster (3m, good to soft) on first occasion; minor honours in Grade 2 events since (hooded last time, not today); reliable and basically progressive but she needs to resume improvement in this hot handicap.

runners.comment: Regular winner, including on two of his three starts this season; up another 6lb
runners.name: Ikarak
runners.owner: Middleham Park Racing & Mrs D J Brown
runners.spotlight: Below form on his only run at this track, albeit two years ago; regular winner, including at Lingfield (2m7f, good to soft) and Ayr (3m, soft) in two of three starts this season, with a creditable third to Kikijo at Sandown in between; up another 6lb but if he's in contention he will be staying on.

runners.comment: Very inconsistent in recent starts but won two of them, including Leopardstown qualifier
runners.name: Duke Silver
runners.spotlight: Hugely hit and miss on his last four starts, the good days when winning over about this trip at Listowel with cheekpieces and at Leopardstown (18-runner qualifier from Yeah Man) without them; heavy ground may excuse latest start; needs to find more but he's just a 6yo, so it may be possible.

runners.comment: Has a much lower hurdles mark; close second to Duke Silver in the Leopardstown qualifier
runners.name: Yeah Man
runners.spotlight: No ground worries; best winning day in the 2024 Grand National Trial at Haydock and he's been placed in last two editions of the Troytown in November; those were over fences but he has a much lower hurdles mark and was a close second to Duke Silver in the Leopardstown qualifier; good chance he'll be outspeeded in this but dangerous if he turns for home in contention.

runners.comment: Fifth hurdle race when justifying favouritism in Naas qualifier (2m7f, heavy) 18 days ago
runners.name: Melbourne Shamrock
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 7yo; fifth race over hurdles when justifying favouritism in the nine-runner Naas qualifier (2m7f, heavy) 18 days ago with cheekpieces fitted for handicap debut, helping to set the pace and holding on by a neck from Minella Sixo; tries blinkers this time; relatively unexposed and probably a thorough stayer, so he should figure in calculations.

runners.comment: 2-4 back hurdling this term; tailed off on latest start; unraced beyond 2m5f under rules
runners.name: Idy Wood
runners.spotlight: Won two chases last season and 2-4 back hurdling this term, with all those wins on good ground but he also scored on soft in his novice days; however, tailed off at Windsor on New Year's Day, unraced beyond 2m5f under rules and needs to resume his improvement.

runners.comment: No shock if he remains capable of better but there is a question over his ideal trip
runners.name: Letos
runners.spotlight: Placed over hurdles/fences in France; six races for Tony Mullins, steadily progressive until tailing off at 22-1 in 2m4f Grade 1 novice on soft going two months ago; 2m4f win in November was sandwiched by seconds over 2m and 3m1f, latterly in a six-runner Carlisle qualifier, and while it would be no shock if he remains capable of better, there is a question over his ideal trip.

runners.comment: Stretched just over 5l ahead from Minella Emperor on the run-in at Haydock (3m) latest
runners.name: Champagne Chic
runners.spotlight: Made debut in January last year and has won three of eight starts, including over about 3m at Wincanton (heavy) and Haydock (good to soft) on last two; 7lb rise since latest demands better still but he keeps finding for pressure and ended up just over 5l ahead last time, stretching on further from Minella Emperor on the run-in; better still could easily be on its way.

runners.breeder: M G Cousin M P Havard Mme J Cousin
runners.comment: 4-4 in handicaps (soft/good to soft) and strode clear for two emphatic wins over about 3m
runners.name: CEst Different
runners.spotlight: 4-4 in handicaps (soft/good to soft) and strode clear for emphatic wins at Market Rasen and Newbury when stepped up to about 3m on his two runs this season; up another 10lb but he's been seeing out those races in grand style and, after just eight starts, still possesses serious potential.

runners.comment: Lightly raced; not that straightforward but there's time for him to get his act together
runners.name: Minella Emperor
runners.spotlight: Won two bumpers on good ground last year; 0-5 over hurdles but minor honours on last four occasions; 6-1, second of 13 to Champagne Chic when upped to 3m for Haydock qualifier (good to soft) on handicap debut last time, renewing his effort but not nearly as strongly as the winner on run-in; not that straightforward but there's time for him to get his act together and cheekpieces (worn in two of his bumpers, not the wins) return.

runners.comment: Second run back with Nicky Henderson; fourth in the 2024 Pertemps Final off 13lb higher
runners.name: Bold Endeavour
runners.spotlight: Back with Nicky Henderson after last season with Laura Morgan; third of six to Ace Of Spades at Huntingdon in January came after a year off and was a partial revival; potentially thrown in if he builds on that, as he was fourth in the 2024 Pertemps Final off 13lb higher; stable going well.

runners.comment: Keeps going up the weights and this return to a left-handed track is a concern
runners.name: Onewaywest
runners.spotlight: Won from the front in 2m3f/2m4f, soft-ground handicaps at Warwick and Wetherby despite jumping out to his right; in contention when falling next time and second to Ace Of Spades at Huntingdon (upped markedly to 3m1f, soft) was creditable, but he keeps going up the weights and this return to a left-handed track is a concern.

runners.comment: Second in the Musselburgh qualifier last time but he's an exposed 8yo
runners.name: Idem
runners.spotlight: Never-dangerous tenth in this race last year; ran creditably on three of his four starts this season, second in the Musselburgh qualifier last time, but he's an exposed 8yo who needs to show something new.

runners.comment: Second to Absolutely Doyen at Wincanton (3m) at Christmas; modest show at Plumpton latest
runners.name: Ike Sport
runners.spotlight: Last won in April 2024; well beaten in the 2m5f handicap here last March; second to Absolutely Doyen at Wincanton (3m, good to soft) at Christmas was best effort this term; ran creditably in the Lanzarote at Kempton (2m5f) next time, before a modest show at Plumpton latest; others look more solid.

17:20.race_name: Rosconn Group Fulke Walwyn Kim Muir Challenge Cup Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Hasn't looked a natural over fences but cheekpieces could help, along with Derek O'Connor
runners.name: Jeriko Du Reponet
runners.spotlight: He hasn't looked a natural in his four chases; however, on the two previous occasions he wore these cheekpieces he ran mighty races in hot handicap hurdles last spring (including runner-up in the Pertemps Final here) and top Irish amateur Derek O'Connor rides today; respected.

runners.comment: Respectable efforts on last two starts and now below his last winning mark; not discounted
runners.name: Monbeg Genius
runners.spotlight: Third in the Ultima here (3m1f, soft) in March 2023; this 10yo has run respectably in the Welsh National (3m6f, good to soft) and Haydock Grand National Trial (3m4f, good to soft) on his last two starts and is now below his last winning mark; not discounted with blinkers replacing cheekpieces.

runners.comment: Not kicked on from impressive novice win in December but not ruled out for top Irish yard
runners.name: The Enabler
runners.spotlight: Impressive over 2m5f at Fairyhouse in December on second chase start; two lesser runs have followed in Grade 3s and there remains a question mark regarding stamina; however, Gordon Elliott and Rob James won this with a 7yo novice in 2020 and he's not ruled out in view of the Fairyhouse promise.

runners.comment: 2m4f third at Musselburgh in January but well beaten there since; stamina a big unknown
runners.name: Insurrection
runners.spotlight: Impressive at Musselburgh (2m4f, good to soft) last February and back to form when third there (2m4f, good to soft) in January; however, this inconsistent 9yo was well beaten at Musselburgh last month and this is a big step into the unknown in terms of stamina (albeit that he did win a 3m point).

runners.comment: Well handicapped on peak form but hasn't produced it in last 12 months; cheekpieces go on
runners.name: Sandor Clegane
runners.owner: Mrs K Browne & Mrs Anne Coffey
runners.spotlight: Promising novice chaser in 2023-24 season and ran well in Graded hurdles in winter 2024-25; well handicapped on his peak form but he's failed to produce it over the last 12 months; 0-9 over fences and last hurdle win was in April 2023; a major turnaround is needed in first-time cheekpieces.

runners.comment: Two-time course winner but over 2m4f and he doesn't appear to be crying out for this trip
runners.name: Il Ridoto
runners.spotlight: Two-time course winner (2m4f, soft/good) who, having dropped down the weights, returned to form when second here on New Year's Day (2m4f, good; albeit no match for the winner); however, he doesn't appear to be crying out for the step up in trip; faded over 3m in February 2024.

runners.breeder: Haras De La Croix Sonnet & S Hosselet
runners.comment: Inconsistent but this novice looks a type who will be suited by the demands of this race
runners.name: Prends Garde A Toi
runners.spotlight: Inconsistent in this novice campaign but ran well when fourth of 14 at Punchestown (3m3f, heavy) last month and that performance can be upgraded, as he was outpaced in the straight in that slowly run race but rallied strongly in the closing stages; it's almost certain there will be a better gallop here and he could be seen to very good effect up the Cheltenham hill.

runners.comment: Has run well here on last three starts, winning most recently; wind op since; solid claims
runners.name: Herakles Westwood
runners.spotlight: Second-season chaser who has run well here on his last three starts, finishing second of 16 under Finian Maguire (3m1f, heavy) then fourth over this C&D (good to soft; lost a shoe) before winning here (3m1f, good) on New Year's Day; has had wind surgery since and he's a solid contender.

runners.comment: Had just 5 rivals to beat at Newbury last time but he was impressive; not ruled out up 6lb
runners.name: Kings Threshold
runners.spotlight: 9yo who has a good strike-rate over fences and produced a career-best performance to win at Newbury (3m2f, good) in December when last seen; has also won on soft ground; had just five rivals to beat on that latest start but he was impressive and is not ruled out now 6lb higher.

runners.comment: Below par latest but good 2nd previously; 4th in this last year; each-way shout if on song
runners.name: Weveallbeencaught
runners.spotlight: Disappointing at Leopardstown in December last time but in good form previously for new yard, finishing second in the Munster National in October (3m, yielding to soft); 13l fourth in this race last year when he'd have been closer but for a bad late mistake; each-way shout if back on song.

runners.comment: Kept on well for close 3rd in big-field handicap over extended 2m5f at Leopardstown latest
runners.name: Waterford Whispers
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in the Martin Pipe Handicap Hurdle here (2m4f, heavy) in March 2024; 0-6 over fences but he returned to form when third in a big-field handicap at Leopardstown (extended 2m5f, soft) last month, when shaping as though this first crack at a staying trip could be right up his street.

runners.comment: Won easily at Aintree in December when back chasing but not in the same good form since
runners.name: Uncle Bert
runners.spotlight: Won at 3m over hurdles at Haydock (soft) last January and scored easily at Aintree (2m4f, soft) in December when back chasing; however, beaten quite some way out in the Welsh National next time (3m6f, good to soft; fell two out) and below par here (2m4f, soft) in January; has to get back on track.

runners.comment: Won this last year; has struggled over hurdles this term but he could go well back here
runners.name: Daily Present
runners.spotlight: Backed into 12-1 when winning this off 6lb lower last year (good to soft) under Barry Stone, when clear with Johnnywho (who won the Ultima on Tuesday off 6lb higher than 12 months ago); pulled up in the Irish National next time and well beaten/pulled up over hurdles on both runs this season, so has something to prove regarding current form, but he could go well back here.

runners.comment: Beginners chase win last March; struggled over hurdles on final 2 runs for Willie Mullins
runners.name: Olympic Man
runners.spotlight: Won 2m4f beginners chase at Naas last March and ran well for a long way in the Scottish National in April (4m) before fading; however, struggled over hurdles on final two runs for Willie Mullins and sold for 16,000gns in January; big revival needed in first-time cheekpieces on stable debut.

runners.comment: Some good form in defeat last year but there's a suspicion he lacks the necessary stamina
runners.name: Excello
runners.spotlight: Very close fourth of six at Sandown last March (3m, good; albeit lost three places close home) and good third over the National fences at Aintree (2m5f, good to soft) in November; however, tailed off there (3m2f, soft) in December and there's a suspicion he'll again be lacking the necessary stamina.

runners.comment: Made all here in December but pulled up on both starts since, the latest only 12 days ago
runners.name: Glengouly
runners.spotlight: Made all here (2m4f, good to soft) in December and remains well handicapped on his old form for Willie Mullins (at up to 3m1f); however, this 10yo has been pulled up on his last two starts, the latest only 12 days ago.

runners.comment: The return to fences and better ground can help; may have potential over a staying trip
runners.name: Road To Home
runners.spotlight: Pulled up over hurdles at Leopardstown (3m, heavy) last month and there's a stamina question to answer; however, his best form has come on good to soft ground over fences and the way he kept on for third at Newbury (2m4f, good to soft) in December hints he may have potential over a staying trip.

runners.comment: Tailed off at 50-1 over hurdles at Haydock last month and looks up against it today
runners.name: Cave Court
runners.spotlight: Runner-up at Cartmel (2m5f, good to soft) last June and he's run well at up to 3m in the past; however, he was tailed off at 50-1 over hurdles at Haydock last month when back from a break and looks up against it today.

runners.comment: 6yo; promise in defeat for new yard and it's possible this new trip will be within range
runners.name: Kim Roque
runners.owner: R A Bartlett/J Carthy/Mrs Paul Shanahan
runners.spotlight: Ex-French 6yo who has shown promise in defeat on his three starts for this yard (soft/good to soft), most recently fifth of 23 over an extended 2m5f at Leopardstown; kept on well when second over 2m6f at Dieppe last June and it's possible this new trip will be within range; might not be far away.

runners.comment: Lightly raced since his second in the 2022 Ultima; second at Ascot latest; possibilities
runners.name: Gericault Roque
runners.owner: Prof Caroline Tisdall And Bryan Drew
runners.spotlight: 10yo who has been lightly raced, with mixed results, since finishing second in the 2022 Ultima here (3m1f, good to soft); however, he returned to form when second at Ascot (3m, good to soft) last month in first-time cheekpieces (retained) and can be in the mix if backing up that effort.

runners.comment: Below best on both outings this winter and now 0-9 over fences; gets a change of headgear
runners.name: No Time To Wait
runners.spotlight: He's on a competitive mark on chase form as recent as last July; however, he hasn't been at his best on either outing this winter and is now 0-9 over fences; needs to raise his game in first-time blinkers (replacing a visor); well beaten in the NH Chase (3m6f) at last season's Festival.

runners.comment: Hat-trick last year on good/good to firm; the drier the ground the better
runners.name: Ask Brewster
runners.spotlight: Hat-trick last year (2m7f/3m4f, good/good to firm) featured a spring win at Cheltenham; ran well for a long way before tiring at Sandown (3m4f) in December on going that was good to soft, soft in places; better ground today would be a plus for his claims.

runners.comment: A return to form is needed from this 11yo but he likes it here; might have an each-squeak
runners.name: Hung Jury
runners.spotlight: Won hunter chase here (4m, good) last May and added a handicap here (3m1f, heavy) in November, before finishing second at Sandown (3m4f, good to soft); pulled up in Welsh National next time and tailed off over hurdles latest, but this 11yo has an each-way squeak if returning to form back here.

runners.comment: In good heart in these blinkers in the autumn but this 11yo may find this too competitive
runners.name: Lord Accord
runners.spotlight: Course winner who scored in first-time blinkers (retained since) at Fontwell (3m2f, good to soft) in October before 11l second at Ascot (3m5f, good); this 11yo returns from a break today and may find this too competitive.

16:49.race_name: bettingsites.co.uk UK Betting Sites Amateur Jockeys' Handicap

runners.comment: Eye-catching finishing effort in 1m Class 5 on h'cap debut; longer trip a plus; intriguing
runners.name: Bronte Beach
runners.spotlight: Top-class pedigree but jettisoned by Godolphin after just one run; seventh in her three runs for Archie Watson but the latest, her handicap debut (1m) where she was an unconsidered 66-1, was a lot more promising than the bare facts; she was poorly positioned in that 0-70 but ran the fastest final 2f split and only beaten 3l at the finish; crying out for the longer distance on breeding and she's an intriguing contender.

runners.comment: Two good runs for new stable, including a C&D win; experienced rider booked; big player
runners.name: Beachborough Girl
runners.spotlight: C&D win on her stable debut in January off 4lb lower; similar form when third at Southwell three weeks later (1m3f); experienced rider on board and she is more appealing than many.

runners.comment: Having a fine winter, including a C&D win; inexperienced amateur booked
runners.name: Silkies Sib
runners.spotlight: Two wins, one over C&D, this winter and he has been a model of consistency since a visor went on; 3lb worse off for a nose with He's Our Cracker on last month's Wolverhampton run; inexperienced amateur on board.

runners.breeder: J Hanly A Stroud & Skymarc Farm
runners.comment: On a dangerous mark and new blinkers could help; second ride for Jack Loughnane
runners.name: Crafter
runners.spotlight: Down to a dangerous mark and although he hasn't fired yet this winter, the addition of blinkers could give him a lift; second ride under rules for Jack Loughnane.

runners.comment: Improved 3rd at Wolverhampton latest; weighted to reverse form with Silkies Sib; unexposed
runners.name: Hes Our Cracker
